text.p: Portuguese cash bonds and futures ended sharply higher, driven up by bullish Spanish Bonos, but dealers said the rise had temporarily run out of steam and the market would now wait for the outcome of the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting.
"The 10-year yield differential with Bunds is less than 60 basis points. This is all thanks to Spain and the fact that the peseta now looks more likely to join the single currency," said one trader.
Dealers said that if Spain made further gains on Wednesday, 10-year spreads under Bonos could narrow slightly.
But they said the Fed's decision at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting would be key.
"Today the 'Club Med' countries virtually ignored the Fed but tomorrow will be a different story," said another dealer.
Traders said the market would not be alarmed by a rise of 25 basis points in short-term U.S. rates.
"It would show that the Fed is serious about combating inflation, it would support the dollar and it would postpone any bigger rate rise," said the first trader.
